introduce:
Start with your knees and hands on the floor. Put your hands a little forward, widen your knees and put your toes together. 

Take a breath, then exhale and sit back. Try to make your butt touch your heels. Relax your elbows, make your forehead touch the floor and try to lower your chest close to the floor. Hold this position.

Keep your arms stretched forward as you sit back. Make sure there is enough space between your shoulders and ears during the exercise.
name: CHILD'S POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please make sure there is enough space between your shoulders and ears.
Please keep your arms stretched forward as you sit back.
This exercise gently stretches your upper back, shoulders, hips and legs.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Lie on the floor with your feet together. Open your knees to the sides. Hold this position.\n\nBreathe in deeply and slowly breathe out.
name: LYING BUTTERFLY STRETCH

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
You should feel a stretch in your groin.
Breathe in deeply and slowly breathe out.
Try to let your knees get closer and closer to the floor.

introduce: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms stretched at your sides. \n\nExhale, lift your knees and twist your legs to the left. Breathe naturally. Hold this position.
name: LYING TWIST STRETCH LEFT

tips.text: You need to do this exercise on a mat.
Please make sure your knees are together.
Please always keep your shoulders on the floor.
Breathe regularly.
You should feel a gentle stretch on your opposite waist.
You shouldn’t feel any pain.
This exercise stretches your obliques and lower back.

introduce: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms stretched at your sides. \n\nExhale, lift your knees and twist your legs to the right. Breathe naturally. Hold this position.
name: LYING TWIST STRETCH RIGHT

tips.text: You need to do this exercise on a mat.
Please make sure your knees are together.
Please always keep your shoulders on the floor.
Breathe regularly.
You should feel a gentle stretch on your opposite waist.
You shouldn’t feel any pain.
This exercise stretches your obliques and lower back.

introduce: Lie down on your back with your legs extended.\n\nBend your knees and bring them up toward your chest; hug your knees with both hands. Breathe naturally. Hold for a few seconds.
name: DOUBLE KNEES TO CHEST

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Hold on your thighs instead if you have knee injuries.
It’s a good exercise to stretch your lower back muscles.
It helps to restore flexibility to your lower back.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Lie on your back with your feet flat on the floor. Put your left ankle on your right knee.\n\nLift your right knee, and grab the back of your right thigh with both hands. Gently pull it towards your body.
name: GLUTE STRETCH LEFT

tips.text: Please relax your hips.
If it’s hard for you, pull your thigh up by holding a towel.
To make a deeper stretch, use one of your hands to push your opposite knee.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Lie on your back with your feet flat on the floor. Put your right ankle on your left knee.\n\nLift your left knee, and grab the back of your left thigh with both hands. Gently pull it towards your body.
name: GLUTE STRETCH RIGHT

tips.text: Please relax your hips.
If it’s hard for you, pull your thigh up by holding a towel.
To make a deeper stretch, use one of your hands to push your opposite knee.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands under your shoulders. 

Bring your left knee forward, place your left foot on the ground between your right hand and right knee and drop your left knee close to your left wrist on the ground. 

Slide your right leg backward. Put your forearms on the ground in front of your leg, with your fingers apart and your palms facing each other. Breathe slowly and deeply. Hold for a few seconds.
name: PIGEON POSE LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Your front knee should be in line with the outside of your shoulder.
You should not feel any discomfort.
This exercise helps to make your muscle groups more flexible.
This exercise helps to reduce sciatic pain.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands under your shoulders. 

Bring your right knee forward, place your right foot on the ground between your left hand and left knee and drop your right knee close to your right wrist on the ground. 

Slide your left leg backward. Put your forearms on the ground in front of your leg, with your fingers apart and your palms facing each other. Breathe slowly and deeply. Hold for a few seconds.
name: PIGEON POSE RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Your front knee should be in line with the outside of your shoulder.
You should not feel any discomfort.
This exercise helps to make your muscle groups more flexible.
This exercise helps to reduce sciatic pain.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground. 

Flatten your lower back on the ground to eliminate the gap between your lower back and the floor, then return to the starting position. 

Repeat the exercise.
name: THE NO-GAP

tips.text: Please do it on a mat.
Squeeze your glutes and flatten your lower back on the ground.
This exercise can help fix the anterior pelvic tilt.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Lie on your back with your legs stretched, hands at your sides and palms up. Take deep relaxation on the floor.\n\nTake deep breaths through your nose. Connect your body to the breath.
name: RELAXATION LYING POSE

tips.text: Close your eyes, relax your arms and legs, relax your face, relax the ankles.
Take deep breaths through your nose.
Let any weight, any tension relax to the earth, feel the floor below you, supporting you.
Let every part of your body relax and lower to the ground.
Invite rest and peace into your mind, body and soul.

introduce: Sit with the soles of your feet together. Draw your heels towards your hips, and press your knees down as much as possible. \n\nPlace your hands in front of you, and try to lean forward. Hold this position.
name: EASY BUTTERFLY POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Press your knees down as much as possible.
Breathe deeply.
Keep your sit bones down.
You should feel the stretch in your thighs.
This position can open up your hips and thighs.
This position helps stretch your thighs.

introduce: Sit on the floor with your feet hip width apart. Lift your arms at shoulder height, curl your chin towards your chest. Reach your hands forward to touch your toes, then return and repeat.\n\nExhale as you reach forward, and inhale as you return. This exercise stretches your calves, hamstrings and back.
name: FORWARD SPINE STRETCH PULSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Exhale as you reach forward, and inhale as you return.
Pull your toes toward your body.
Bring your shoulders down away from your ears.
This exercise stretches your calves, hamstrings and back.

introduce:
Start on your knees and elbows. Place your elbows under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. 

Drop your head on the floor, and put your hands on the top of your head. Round your spine while keeping your upper back still. 

Inhale, and drop your pelvis down. Exhale, and round your spine. Repeat the exercise.
name: LUMBAR CAT COW

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your upper back still during exercise.
Inhale as you drop your pelvis down, and exhale as you round your spine.
This exercise can mobilize your lumbar spine.

introduce:
Lie on your stomach with your legs extended. Spread your arms out to the sides with your palms down on the ground.

Lift your left leg off the floor and cross it over to your right side, trying to touch your toes to the floor.

Return to the starting position, and repeat with the other side.
name: PRONE SCORPION KICKS

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please exercise within your range of motion to avoid straining your lower back.
This exercise stretches your hip flexors and lower back.
Breathe regularly.

introduce: Sit on the floor. Bend your knees, put your hands on your shins and hold your knees close to your chest.\n\nKeep your spine rounded, then gently swing back and forth. Exhale as you roll forward, and inhale as you roll backward.
name: SPINAL ROLLING

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your spine rounded.
Engage your core to keep balance.
Don\'t roll back too far on your neck.
Keep the movement controlled.
Exhale as you roll forward, and inhale as you roll backward.
This exercise can loosen up your spine and relieve your back pain.

introduce:
Sit upright on the floor. Bend your left leg with your heel close to your sit bone. 

Extend your right leg. Put your left hand on the floor behind you. 

Exhale, twist your upper body to the left. Bend your right elbow with your fingers pointing to the ceiling. Fix your right elbow on the outside of your left knee. 

Turn your gaze over your left shoulder. Hold this position.
name: SAGE MARICHI'S POSE Ⅲ LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your back straight.
Keep your legs still when twisting your body.
Twist from your waist instead of your chest.
Evenly distribute your weight between both sit bones.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Breathe naturally.
If sitting upright is challenging, place a block under your buttocks.
This exercise stretches your shoulders, chest, and spine.
This exercise helps relieve your back and hip pain.

introduce:
Sit upright on the floor. Bend your right leg with your heel close to your sit bone. 

Extend your left leg. Put your right hand on the floor behind you. 

Exhale, twist your upper body to the right. Bend your left elbow with your fingers pointing to the ceiling. Fix your left elbow on the outside of your right knee. 

Turn your gaze over your right shoulder. Hold this position.
name: SAGE MARICHI'S POSE Ⅲ RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your back straight.
Keep your legs still when twisting your body.
Twist from your waist instead of your chest.
Evenly distribute your weight between both sit bones.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Breathe naturally.
If sitting upright is challenging, place a block under your buttocks.
This exercise stretches your shoulders, chest, and spine.
This exercise helps relieve your back and hip pain.

introduce:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Turn your toes outwards. Bring your hands together into a prayer position in front of you. 

Bend your knees and lower your body as much as you can. Press your elbows against your inner knees to open up your hips. 

Keep your heels on the floor, if you can't, place a rolled-up towel under your heels. 

Breathe in deeply and breathe out completely. Hold this position.
name: GARLAND POSE

tips.text: Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Breathe naturally.
This exercise stretches your groins, lower back, and hips.
This exercise strengthens and stretches your ankles.

introduce:
Lie on your back. Bring your knees close to your chest with the soles of your feet towards the ceiling. 

Grab the inside of your feet. Slightly open your knees wider than your torso and bring them towards your armpits. 

Breathe naturally. Hold this position.
name: HAPPY BABY POSE

tips.text: Please do this on the mat.
Breathe naturally.
Keep your head on the mat to avoid neck strain.
This exercise can help relieve your lower back pain.
This exercise stretches your inner thighs, hamstrings, groin, and spine.
